rule: Title tag must be between 50-60 characters
principle: Titles outside 50-60 chars get rewritten by Google, losing keyword placement control

rule: Meta description must not exceed 160 characters
principle: Google truncates descriptions over 160 chars; bolded keyword matches in snippet boost CTR

rule: Primary keyword must appear within the first 60 characters of the title tag
principle: Google weights front-loaded keywords more heavily; users instantly recognize relevance

rule: URL must contain descriptive, human-readable words relevant to page content
principle: URLs appear as breadcrumbs in SERPs; descriptive URLs help users judge relevance pre-click

rule: Page must implement structured data markup (JSON-LD) appropriate to content type
principle: Schema markup enables rich results, AI citations, and helps Google understand entity types

rule: Blog posts must include Article or BlogPosting schema with datePublished, author, and headline
principle: Article schema enables Top Stories eligibility, better title display, and date visibility

rule: Pages answering buyer questions must have FAQPage schema markup with at least 3 Question/Answer pairs
principle: FAQ schema is the highest-signal AEO markup — it feeds AI Overviews, featured snippets, and voice search

rule: Every page must contain at least 3 internal links to other relevant pages on the same domain
principle: Internal links distribute PageRank, signal content relationships to crawlers, and reduce orphan pages

rule: Link anchor text must be descriptive and relevant, never generic phrases like 'click here' or 'learn more'
principle: Anchor text tells Google what the linked page is about — generic text forfeits ranking signal

rule: Content pages must exceed 1500 words to demonstrate topical authority
principle: Google and AI engines correlate content depth with authority; thin content rarely ranks or gets cited

rule: Content must use a logical heading hierarchy (H1 > H2 > H3) to facilitate LLM scanning and chunking
principle: LLMs chunk content by headings for retrieval; proper hierarchy increases citation probability

rule: Primary keyword must appear within the first 100 words of body content
principle: Early keyword presence signals relevance immediately to both crawlers and readers

rule: Content must provide unique information gain not found in top 3 SERP competitors (original data, case studies, local insights)
principle: Information gain is the strongest ranking signal in 2026; AI engines preferentially cite unique content

rule: Content must be written for humans first — natural language, no keyword stuffing, answers user intent
principle: Google's Helpful Content System demotes content written for search engines, not people

rule: Page must be mobile-responsive with no horizontal scroll or unreadable text on mobile viewport
principle: Google uses mobile-first indexing; non-responsive pages lose rankings across all devices

rule: Page must not have intrusive interstitials or ads that obstruct primary content
principle: Intrusive interstitials trigger Google's penalty since 2017; hurts mobile rankings specifically

rule: All content images must have descriptive alt text containing relevant keywords
principle: Alt text enables image search visibility, accessibility compliance, and provides keyword context

rule: Site must have an XML sitemap submitted to Google Search Console
principle: Sitemaps are the most reliable way to ensure all pages get crawled, especially for new/large sites

rule: Content mentioning 'Texas' must also mention relevant cities (Houston, Katy, Austin, Dallas)
principle: Entity co-occurrence signals geographic relevance to Google; missing cities = weak local SEO

rule: Content discussing buyer topics must clearly state Quan represents buyers
principle: Clear positioning differentiates from listing agents and establishes trust with buyer audience

rule: Every page must have a clear, visible path to schedule a consultation or contact Quan
principle: Without a conversion path, SEO traffic generates no business value — every page is a landing page

rule: Katy-targeted pages must include Katy-specific market context, not generic Texas real estate content
principle: Local specificity is the strongest local SEO signal; generic content loses to hyperlocal competitors

rule: Pages targeting first-time buyers must cover core entities: Buyer's Agent, Closing Costs, Down Payment Assistance, Home Inspection, Mortgage Pre-approval
principle: Entity completeness signals topical authority; missing key buyer entities = Google sees thin coverage
